column2: For every finite set V and every binary relation A⊆V×V, both Γ_A and Γ_B terminate at the same reflexive, symmetric, transitive closure Eq(A). Thus their terminal normal-form maps are extensionally identical.

Repeated one-step closure adds all finite-path consequences; finite V gives termination.

column1: 1. Eq(A) is an equivalence relation containing A by construction.
2. Any equivalence relation E containing A must contain every finite A-path pair, because transitivity propagates along paths. Hence Eq(A)⊆E.
3. Γ_B explicitly computes reflexive + symmetric + transitive closure, so Γ_B(A)=Eq(A).
4. Γ_A is extensive and monotone. Each iteration adds relational consequences generated by Boolean composition and reflexive/symmetric closure.
5. On a finite V there are only |V|^2 possible ordered pairs, so the ascending chain A⊆Γ_A(A)⊆Γ_A^2(A)⊆… stabilizes after finitely many steps.
6. At stabilization F=Γ_A(F), so F is reflexive and symmetric and is closed under the relational composition used by τ. Hence F is transitive.
7. Therefore F is an equivalence relation containing A, so Eq(A)⊆F.
8. Conversely every Γ_A iteration adds only consequences already contained in Eq(A); by induction Γ_A^n(A)⊆Eq(A). Thus F⊆Eq(A).
9. Therefore F=Eq(A), proving Γ_A^*(A)=Eq(A)=Γ_B(A), and hence Γ_A^*(A)=Γ_B^*(A).
